A security vulnerability has been detected in itsourcecode Insurance Management System 1.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file /deleteClient.php. Such manipulation of the argument client_id leads to sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

A flaw has been found in Microweber up to 2.0.20. This impacts the function UserManager::make_logged of the file src/MicroweberPackages/App/Http/Controllers/ApiController.php of the component Generic API Dispatcher. This manipulation causes improper access controls. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.0.21 will fix this issue. Patch name: e639d26e61b989b100f8b6f6bb78c0cecca79b99. You should upgrade the affected component.

A flaw was found in Quay. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker holding a restricted, short-lived JSON Web Token (JWT) to achieve privilege escalation. Because Quay improperly accepts scoped registry bearer tokens as valid robot account passwords, an attacker can authenticate directly as the robot account and obtain broader permissions. Consequently, unauthorized access persists and enables the attacker to generate fresh tokens even after the robot account's password has been reset.

Mailflare before 48957fb contains a host header injection vulnerability in the password-reset request handler that allows unauthenticated attackers to poison reset links when APP_URL is unset. Attackers can submit a reset request for a victim's email with a malicious Host header, capturing the single-use token when the victim clicks the link to take over the account.

Open5GS AMF through 2.8.0 contains a missing resource release vulnerability that allows authenticated UEs to orphan SMF sessions by triggering Create SM Context response processing failures. Attackers can repeatedly release the RAN UE context while responses are pending, causing AMF_SESS_CLEAR() without Release SM Context requests and degrading SMF availability.

OpenAirInterface CN5G PCF through 2.2.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in pcf_smpc::delete_sm_policy_handler() that leaves stale UE IPv4, SUPI and DNN index entries after association deletion. Attackers can trigger repeated SM policy create and delete cycles over N7 via PDU session establishment and release to grow PCF memory without bound and break association lookups.

free5GC SMF through 1.4.6 contains a missing resource release vulnerability in HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate that leaves CHF charging sessions open when PCF session rule application fails. Attackers can repeatedly trigger failed PDU session establishments to accumulate orphaned charging sessions on the CHF and degrade its availability.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in xmt_parse_command() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that casts target nodes to GF_ParentNode without validation. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT-A file whose command targets a non-grouping node, causing gf_node_list_get_child() to perform an invalid memory read and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a double free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader that leaves a stale GF_Command pointer in a Conditional node's SFCommandBuffer when the buffer element is not properly closed. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file with malformed nesting, causing gf_sg_sfcommand_del() to free the live command, corrupting heap memory and crashing the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that retains a pointer to a PROTO sub-graph freed by gf_sg_proto_del(). Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file imported with MP4Box, causing xmt_parse_command() to update the freed graph's referencing_commands list and crash the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in src/compositor/mpeg4_sensors.c that allows attackers to crash the process via uninitialized sensor nodes. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that makes compositor_mpeg4_get_sensor_handler_ex() call hs->IsEnabled through a near-NULL pointer, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader because xmt_node_end() frees unattached nodes but leaves them on the parser node stack. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file whose text content makes xmt_text_content() pass the freed node to gf_node_get_tag(), reading freed heap memory and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in xmt_resolve_od_links() that allows attackers to corrupt stack memory via over-long object descriptor URL fragments. Attackers can craft an XMT scene file whose URL fragment overflows the fixed 5000-byte szURL buffer via sprintf, crashing MP4Box when a user loads it.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory when xmt_node_end() discards an out-of-scope node without resetting command-buffer state. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file that leaves parser->command_buffer and parser->command dangling, causing later parsing to access freed memory and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap-based buffer over-read vulnerability in gf_xml_sax_peek_node() in src/utils/xml_parser.c that lets attackers read past the heap line buffer. Attackers can craft an XMT file whose ROUTE or command references a later-defined node, crashing MP4Box when a user imports it.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT-A scene loader that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted XMT files. Attackers can persuade a user to process an XMT file whose discarded out-of-scope nodes cause gf_node_unregister() to dereference a freed child, crashing the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in xmt_discard_subtree() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to exhaust the call stack. Attackers can persuade a user to process a crafted XMT file with deeply nested discarded SFNode and MFNode fields to crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_resolve_od_links() in loader_xmt.c that allows attackers to read freed heap memory via stale strstr() pointers. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file whose MFURL field contains an entry without a URL string, causing sprintf() to read freed memory and crash the process.

Servas before 1.2.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to modify and delete other users' data by supplying target resource ids. Attackers can abuse TagController update and destroy, LinkController destroy, and GroupController destroy actions to rename or delete tags and delete links and groups.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to access freed heap memory via stale object descriptor links. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene where xmt_node_end() frees a subtree containing InputSensor MFURL fields, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory and crash MP4Box.

Freedit before 0.9.9 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the edit_post_post handler for POST /post/edit/:pid that skips ownership and status checks when a Private inn is submitted. Members of a Private inn can overwrite any post by sequential id, including moderator-locked posts, re-attributing it to themselves and destroying original content.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in TraverseForm() in src/compositor/mpeg4_form.c due to an off-by-one groupsIndex bounds check. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with a Form node having constraints but an empty groupsIndex field to crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_instantiate() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c that lacks cycle detection or depth limits. Attackers can craft an XMT scene whose PROTO body instantiates itself directly or indirectly, exhausting the stack and crashing MP4Box when imported.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in scene graph teardown that allows attackers to trigger access to freed memory via crafted scene files. A node shared across multiple PROTO node_code lists is freed by gf_sg_reset(), and gf_sg_proto_del() then calls gf_node_unregister() on the dangling pointer, crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that leaves freed node URL fields in the pending object descriptor link list after SFNode replacement. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that reassigns a single-node field, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory, crashing the process and potentially corrupting the heap.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c that misinterprets single node values as child lists for MFNode field replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene that causes an invalid node pointer to be dereferenced by gf_node_register(), crashing MP4Box for denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_sg_command_apply() in src/scenegraph/commands.c when handling MFNode field replace commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with an MFNode field replace command lacking a node value to crash MP4Box, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in JSScript_LoadVRML() in src/scenegraph/vrml_js.c that reads unchecked script_text pointers of Script node url entries. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene loading a Script node whose url entry lacks script text, crashing MP4Box and causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the application by supplying a crafted XMT scene. Attackers can modify InputSensor, Layout or EnvironmentTest nodes during parsing, triggering compositor handlers that read uninitialized private stacks and cause denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in gf_event_target_get_node() because destroyed node event targets remain in media object lists. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with nodes such as InputSensor to trigger freed memory reads during gf_scene_disconnect(), crashing the process or corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_create_node() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c when cloning PROTO instances. Attackers can craft an XMT scene declaring more PROTO interface fields than the cloned instance supplies, crashing MP4Box when a user opens the file.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in avi_parse_input_file() in src/media_tools/avilib.c that increments track counters before checking AVI_MAX_TRACKS. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file declaring a ninth audio stream, causing AVI_audio_format and AVI_close() to access track[8] and crash the process.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_del that allows attackers to free PROTOs still owned by another scene command via the GF_SG_PROTO_DELETE handler. Attackers can craft an XMT scene that declares a PROTO in one command and deletes it by ID in another, crashing MP4Box and corrupting heap memory when opened.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in ctxload_process() in src/filters/load_bt_xmt.c that casts object descriptor update entries without checking the descriptor tag. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BT scene placing a different descriptor type in a GF_ODUpdate command, causing gf_list_get() to dereference an invalid pointer and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in src/compositor/mpeg4_text.c that allows heap out-of-bounds reads by casting a Text node's fontStyle field to M_FontStyle unchecked. Attackers can craft an XMT/BIFS scene placing a smaller node like Face in fontStyle, causing build_text to read past the allocation and crash MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT loader that allows scene commands to reference PROTO sub-graph nodes freed by a scene replace command. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file that causes gf_node_get_field() and gf_node_unregister() to access freed memory, crashing MP4Box and potentially corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in curve2d_check_changes() that casts a Curve2D point field node to M_Coordinate2D without type checking. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BIFS scene placing another node type such as LinearGradient in that field, causing an invalid pointer read that crashes the process.

OpenShot Video Editor (openshot-qt) through 4.1.1 contains an unsafe deserialization vulnerability in ProjectDataStore.load() and read_legacy_project_file() that passes non-JSON project files to pickle.load() without restriction. Attackers can trick users into opening a crafted .osp project file containing a pickle __reduce__ gadget to execute code with the user's privileges.

A security vulnerability has been detected in xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. The affected element is the function insert/update of the file admin/src/main/java/com/xxl/job/admin/business/controller/JobGroupController.java of the component Group Management. The manipulation of the argument addressList leads to cross-site request forgery. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Insurance Management System 1.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /insertClient.php. The manipulation of the argument client_id results in sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.

A flaw has been found in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.5. This affects the function ASEImporter::InternReadFile of the file code/AssetLib/ASE/ASELoader.cpp of the component ASE File Importer. This manipulation causes out-of-bounds write. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 6.0.6 mitigates this issue. Patch name: 7ccc44a338dcdcc81023484388126ab1a8250e94. You should upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability has been found in itsourcecode Event Management System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file booking.php. Such manipulation of the argument venue_id leads to cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

A vulnerability was found in Webkul Bagisto up to 2.4.13. Affected is the function RazorpayController::paymentSuccess of the file packages/Webkul/Razorpay/src/Http/Controllers/RazorpayController.php of the component Payment Gateway Success/Callback Controllers. Performing a manipulation results in insufficient verification of data authenticity. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. Upgrading to version 2.4.14 is able to address this issue. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability was determined in Webkul Bagisto up to 2.4.12. Affected by this vulnerability is the function Success of the file packages/Webkul/PayU/src/Http/Controllers/PayUController.php of the component Payu Payment Gateway. Executing a manipulation of the argument Status can lead to insufficient verification of data authenticity. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. Upgrading to version 2.4.13 addresses this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

Members WordPress plugin by MemberPress 3.2.28 before 3.3.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to evade Private Site mode via login page exemption. Attackers can request the front-end login path with a pagename query variable to make WordPress render hidden published pages or the full blog index.

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read comments on role-restricted posts via the Latest Comments block. Attackers can view pages hosting the block, where get_the_ID() checks the host page and get_comment_excerpt() bypasses filtering, exposing restricted comments, post titles, and links.

Members WordPress plugin before 3.3.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated visitors to read role-restricted posts by viewing Latest Posts blocks in full-content mode. The block renders raw post_content without firing the_content filter, bypassing members_content_permissions_protect() and exposing complete bodies of restricted posts.

WPGSI: Spreadsheet Integration before 3.8.5 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to delete posts by abusing the delete action in wpgsi_show_view() without nonce verification. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into following a crafted wpgsi-show link with action=delete and an id parameter to delete arbitrary posts or pages.

anacrolix/torrent before 1.62.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Decoder.readOneValue in bencode/decode.go that allows attackers to crash the process by supplying deeply nested bencode data. Attackers can deliver crafted .torrent files or magnet link metadata with millions of nested lists to cause a fatal stack overflow, or deeply nested v2 file trees to exhaust CPU.

better-chatbot before 2.0.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that lets built-in tools run without user confirmation in Manual tool mode, because src/app/api/chat/route.ts keeps their execute handlers. Attackers can plant prompt-injected documents or web pages that make the HTTP request tool send conversation data to attacker-controlled URLs.

Anacrolix torrent before 1.63.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in NewClient within tracker/http/client.go, which unconditionally sets InsecureSkipVerify to true for HTTPS trackers. Attackers able to intercept tracker traffic can impersonate trackers with any certificate, observe info_hash and peer_id values, and return forged peer lists.

libical before 4.0.7 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in icalparser_clean() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying truncated iCalendar input. Attackers can provide an iCalendar file or stream missing a matching END line, causing the returned component to be freed twice and crashing applications.

FreeRDP before 3.33.1 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the WinPR wLinkedList collection because LinkedList_FreeNode() frees nodes without updating the cached list->current enumerator pointer. When calling code removes the node the enumerator references, LinkedList_Enumerator_MoveNext() or LinkedList_Enumerator_Current() reads freed heap memory, which can crash the process.

Ground Station before 0.8.25 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator operators to write files outside data/decoded via the post_process_pipeline value. Attackers can insert ../ sequences into a scheduled observation's IQ task configuration so SatDump creates directories, overwrites same-named files, and recursively deletes created trees on failure.

Kirby 5.0.0 before 5.6.4 contains a race condition in Kirby\Api\Upload::processChunk() that allows authenticated users with upload permission to bypass SVG sanitization. Attackers can race concurrent chunked uploads sharing a filename to swap a benign SVG with a script-bearing SVG, executing stored cross-site scripting in the site origin.

A weakness has been identified in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.6. The affected element is the function Assimp::ColladaLoader::CreateAnimation of the file code/AssetLib/Collada/ColladaLoader.cpp of the component Collada Loader. This manipulation of the argument mSize causes out-of-bounds write. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.6. The impacted element is the function Assimp::JoinVerticesProcess::ProcessMesh of the file code/PostProcessing/JoinVerticesProcess.cpp of the component PostProcessing JoinVerticesProcess. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was detected in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.5. This affects the function Assimp::PretransformVertices::BuildMeshRefCountArray of the file PretransformVertices.cpp. Performing a manipulation results in out-of-bounds write. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in Open Asset Import Library Assimp up to 6.0.6. This impacts the function Assimp::ColladaLoader::CreateMesh of the file code/AssetLib/Collada/ColladaLoader.cpp. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A vulnerability has been found in xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. Affected is the function difyWorkflowJobHandler of the file xxl-job-executor-sample-springboot-ai/src/main/java/com/xxl/job/executor/jobhandler/AIXxlJob.java of the component AI Executor. The manipulation of the argument baseUrl leads to server-side request forgery. The attack may be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in DumbWareio DumbDrop up to ff8f813f493e89c7da056e7a3101ce2ef48e3960. Affected by this vulnerability is the function isPathWithinUploadDir of the file src/routes/files.js of the component Files API. The manipulation results in improper access controls. The attack may be launched remotely. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in Bagisto MangoPay Payment Gateway up to c061edcc7973cb37a77a9f9ae523db170c3e28ed. Affected by this vulnerability is the function MangoPayStandardController::success of the file src/Http/Controllers/Shop/MangoPayStandardController.php of the component Success Callback. The manipulation leads to insufficient verification of data authenticity. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. This product follows a rolling release approach for continuous delivery, so version details for affected or updated releases are not provided.

A vulnerability has been found in Xuxueli xxl-job 3.5.0/3.5.1-SNAPSHOT. The affected element is an unknown function of the file JobLogController.java of the component Job Termination Endpoint. The manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in code-projects Intern Record System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file /department.sql. Such manipulation leads to file and directory information exposure. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

A security flaw has been discovered in warpdesign pcx-js up to 1.1.1. Affected is the function decode8bpp/decode4bpp of the file js/pcx.js of the component PCX Pixel Buffer Decoder. Performing a manipulation results in uncontrolled memory allocation. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in DumbWareio DumbAssets up to 1.0.11. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file server.js of the component Settings API. Executing a manipulation of the argument appriseUrl can lead to dynamically-determined object attributes. The attack can be executed remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Electerm before 5.9.0 on Windows contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to execute PowerShell code via crafted file or folder names containing Unicode quote characters. Attackers can deliver names containing U+2019 through archives, WSL distributions, or SMB shares, which break out of getFolderSizeWin() and calcLocal() quoting when victims request folder sizes, executing code as the electerm user.

graphql-core 3.2.12 before 3.2.14 and 3.3.0rc1 before 3.3.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass the parser max_tokens limit using long runs of comments. Attackers can submit GraphQL documents of consecutive comments that Lexer.lookahead fully tokenizes before limit checks, consuming CPU and memory proportional to document size.

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the GET /api/v1/assets/*filepath route that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass URL signature checks by prefixing paths with profiles/. Attackers who know a private upload's storage key can request profiles/../users/<id>/<uuid>.<ext> to retrieve private attachments without a signature or login.

Donetick before 0.1.86 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to delete other users' files by storing a crafted image value via PUT /api/v1/users. Attackers can set their image to a traversal key and upload a new profile photo, causing storage.Delete to remove other users' attachments or photos under the storage root.

ByteStash 1.5.0 before 1.6.1 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the /api/auth/oidc/callback handler because OIDC state is not bound to the initiating browser. Attackers can start an OIDC login with their own account and lure victims into opening the withheld callback URL, logging them into the attacker's account to read saved snippets.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because the POST /reset_password/passkey/end handler never calls endUserSessions(). Attackers holding a stolen session cookie keep authenticated access to the victim's account even after the victim recovers it by registering a new passkey.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an improper verification vulnerability that allows authenticated users to retain the emailVerified flag by changing their email address while EMAIL_VERIFICATION is disabled. Attackers with a previously verified account can set another person's address via the PATCH /email handler, receiving OIDC email_verified=true claims to impersonate that owner in relying applications.

VoidAuth before 1.19.2 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade stricter ProxyAuth domain rules by sending percent-encoded path separators. Attackers can request paths with encoded slashes, backslashes, semicolons, or dot segments that match a broader rule, reaching restricted paths once the reverse proxy or backend decodes them.

Portainer 2.39.0 before 2.39.9, 2.40.0 before 2.45.4, and 3.0.0 before 3.1.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows Standard users to access other users' containers via the WebSocket attach and exec endpoints. Attackers with shared environment access can use leaked container or exec IDs to hijack sessions over /api/websocket/attach or /api/websocket/exec, gaining interactive root shells.

Zipline before 4.8.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated OIDC users to make the server fetch arbitrary URLs via the userinfo picture claim. Attackers who control their picture claim at the identity provider can force fetchToDataURL() to request internal or cloud-metadata URLs and read responses from their stored avatar.

Opencast before 20.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in WorkspaceImpl.toWorkspaceFile that allows authenticated ingest users to write files outside the workspace root via unvalidated element paths. Attackers can submit media packages whose element URIs or identifiers contain ../ sequences, causing Workspace.get to create directories and write fetched content with Opencast process privileges.

Gogs before 0.14.4 on Windows contains a path equivalence vulnerability in isRepositoryGitPath that allows authenticated users with write access to bypass .git directory protection using NTFS aliases. Attackers can create, rename or upload files via aliases like git~1 or .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION to overwrite .git/config or hooks and execute commands as the Gogs process.

OpenOLAT 20.2.2 before 20.3.12, 21.0.0 before 21.0.7, and 21.1.0 before 21.1.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the TranscodingDeliveryDispatcher notifyResult callback endpoint. Unauthenticated attackers can POST crafted TranscoderJobResult JSON with attacker-supplied URLs to overwrite transcoded video and audio files and force server-side requests.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a path traversal (zip slip) vulnerability in ImportService#unzip_photos_file that allows authenticated users to write files outside the extraction folder. Attackers can upload a crafted photos zip archive during account import with ../ entry names to create new files at arbitrary locations writable by the diaspora* process.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in Notifier#invite that allows authenticated users to inject HTML or markdown into invitation emails through unescaped profile names. Attackers can set profile first or last names containing raw HTML, links, or images so invitation emails sent from the pod render spoofed content in recipients' mail clients.

msgpackr before 2.1.4 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote attackers to cause denial of service by repeatedly re-decoding buffered incomplete values. Attackers can stream a large container of small elements in small chunks to UnpackrStream or decodeIter, triggering quadratic decoding cost that blocks the Node.js event loop.

Faye websocket-driver 0.5.0 before 0.8.0, permessage-deflate before 0.2.0, and websocket-extensions before 0.2.0 contain a decompression bomb vulnerability because messages are fully inflated before maxLength is enforced. Unauthenticated remote clients negotiating permessage-deflate can send highly compressible messages, forcing processIncomingMessage() to allocate excessive memory and crash the server process.

binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption(). Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled.

simple-git before 4.1.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the allowUnsafePack guard by supplying the --exec option to non-push git operations. Attackers who influence arguments passed to listRemote() or raw() can inject --exec for ls-remote, archive, fetch-pack or send-pack to execute commands on the host.

mcp-server-kubernetes before 4.2.0 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows remote MCP clients to inject kubectl flags by supplying dash-prefixed values as positional operands in tools such as exec_in_pod, kubectl_patch, and kubectl_logs. Attackers connected over SSE or Streamable HTTP transport can supply values like --filename to make kubectl read files from the server host, bypassing file-read restrictions.

oasdiff 1.24.0 before 1.34.1 fails to enforce --allow-external-refs=false when --open is used, because the recordingReader() capture reader in load/capture.go never applies the external-reference policy. Attackers supplying an untrusted OpenAPI spec can use external $ref values to read local files or trigger HTTP requests, with contents uploaded in the review bundle.

Delta Sharing reference server 1.4.0 before 1.5.0 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows share recipients to read unshared data via container-scoped Azure SAS tokens. Recipients with a valid bearer token can request credentials from the temporary-table-credentials endpoint to read every blob in the storage container, including unshared tables.

Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in the pure-Python ASGI parser that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to desynchronize request framing by sending malformed framing headers. Attackers can send whitespace-padded Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length headers, signed Content-Length values, or invalid chunk terminators to smuggle requests past front-end proxies to the ASGI application.

Gunicorn 25.2.0 before 27.0.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the pure-Python ASGI HTTP/1 parser that buffers protocol lines without size limits. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send request lines, headers, chunk-size lines or trailers lacking CRLF to grow worker memory and consume CPU, causing denial of service.

Sustainsys.Saml2 before 1.0.4 and 2.x before 2.11.1 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability that allows attackers to tamper with signed parameters by exploiting mis-parsing in CheckSignature() of Saml2RedirectBinding.cs. Attackers can append data after an extra '=' in RelayState of an intercepted or replayed Redirect-binding message, causing applications to trust the tampered value.

Kitty 0.43.0 before 0.51.0 contains a terminal escape sequence injection vulnerability that allows attackers to emit escape sequences by crafting malicious file or archive member names. When a victim highlights such an entry in the choose-files kitten preview panel, unsanitized names are written raw, enabling OSC 52 clipboard overwrites, OSC 8 links, window title changes, or screen spoofing.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.98 contains a link following vulnerability that allows malicious repositories to read host files by setting --eventpath in an untrusted project .actrc to a symlink. Attackers can commit an event.json symlink pointing to files like ~/.ssh/id_rsa, which act copies into the job container as GITHUB_EVENT_PATH for workflow steps to exfiltrate.

erxes before 3.4.14 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the insurance_api plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to create, overwrite or delete contract templates via GraphQL mutations. Attackers can inject HTML into templates rendered by headless Chromium during generateContractPDF to pull internal network content into PDFs and exfiltrate customer fields.

Lightdash before 3.212.0 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability in getGitlabInstallationRepoReadAccess that sends the organization GitLab app token to unverified hosts. Project developers can set the dbt connection host_domain to an attacker-controlled server and capture the token when the AI agent reads the repository, gaining access to every reachable repository.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.19.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the sanitize-svg function that allows authenticated users to bypass filtering through unescaped re-serialization. Attackers with file edit permission can upload SVGs using entity-encoded or CDATA-wrapped markup or attribute quote breakouts to execute JavaScript in the Penpot origin when victims open them.

Umami 3.3.0 before 3.5.0 contains a race condition in two-factor authentication attempt limiting that allows attackers holding a user's password to bypass lockout. Attackers can send many concurrent POST requests to /api/2fa/verify that pass checkRateLimit before recordFailedAttempt runs, brute-forcing TOTP or backup codes beyond the five-attempt limit.

Casdoor before 4.27.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in decodeSamlMessage that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by sending unbounded DEFLATE-compressed SAML messages. Attackers can send a small, highly compressed SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse to the /api/saml/logout/:owner/:application endpoint, which inflates to gigabytes and crashes or stalls the server.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read unpublished help center articles through the public portal API. Attackers can request archived articles by slug via the ArticlesController show actions or read draft translations exposed through associated_articles in article JSON responses.

Vim 9.2.0405 before 9.2.1352 contains a security bypass vulnerability in expand_tag_fname() that allows attackers to evade 'tagsecure' URL checks by escaping URLs in tags file entries. Attackers can supply a crafted tags file in a cloned repository so that jumping to a tag makes netrw fetch an attacker-controlled URL leaking environment variable values.

RSSHub before 2026.11.01-8521.e529e9b contains a domain validation bypass in the javdb routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to capture the operator's JAVDB_SESSION cookie. Attackers can pass an absolute javdb.com URL in the category parameter and set the domain query to a host they control, causing processItems to send the _jdb_session cookie there.

Langfuse before 4.82.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows organization admins to target internal hosts by setting the GitHub Enterprise SSO baseUrl, which skips outbound-URL validation. Attackers can point baseUrl to loopback, RFC1918, or cloud metadata addresses so user sign-ins trigger server requests carrying stored OAuth client credentials.

Dashy 4.0.0 before 4.9.12 contains a credential disclosure vulnerability in isLocalRequest that attaches user credentials to lookalike hosts due to prefix-only origin checks. Attackers can lure logged-in users to a crafted ?config= link pointing to a lookalike host, capturing bearer tokens or HTTP auth headers to read configuration and stored API keys, or modify them when the victim is an admin.

Frappe before 15.126.0 and 16.x before 16.55.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows Dashboard Manager users to pollute Object.prototype by storing __proto__ keys in Dashboard Chart custom_options. When any user, including administrators, views a dashboard rendering the chart, Object.assign merges attacker properties into Object.prototype, altering Frappe desk client behavior for that session.

Weblate before 2026.11 contains an account takeover vulnerability in the reset_password view that allows unauthenticated attackers to reset victim passwords by abusing case-insensitive Unicode e-mail matching. Attackers controlling a lookalike mailbox using a dotless i or other case-folding variant receive the victim's reset link, since it is sent to the typed address, and set a new password.

HumHub before 1.19.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in GroupController actionNewMemberSearch and actionAdminUserSearch, which skip the checkGroupAccess check. A manager of any single group can query admin-user-search and new-member-search with another group's id parameter to enumerate members, including administrators.

A security vulnerability has been detected in aceberg WatchYourLAN up to 2.1.4. Affected by this issue is the function getPortState of the file backend/internal/api/api-network.go of the component Web API. The manipulation of the argument addr leads to server-side request forgery. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was detected in leonkhoo123 self-hosting-file-uploader up to 473e38ff8fba494f33a485730c6d95c5d8c536ea. This affects an unknown part of the file routes/generator.js of the component Admin Generator API. The manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack may be performed from remote. This product utilizes a rolling release system for continuous delivery, and as such, version information for affected or updated releases is not disclosed.

A flaw has been found in shaozilee bmp-js up to 0.1.0. This vulnerability affects the function BmpDecoder.parseRGBA of the file lib/decoder.js. This manipulation causes uncontrolled memory allocation. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability has been found in vthibault tga-js up to 1.1.1. This issue affects the function _decodeRLE of the file src/tga.js of the component TgaLoader. Such manipulation leads to uncontrolled memory allocation. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability was found in andreasgal node-wav up to 0.0.2. Impacted is the function decode of the file index.js of the component WAV Decoder. Performing a manipulation results in uncontrolled memory allocation. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was determined in kchapelier qoijs 1.0.0. The affected element is the function decode of the file src/decode.js of the component QOI Decoder. Executing a manipulation of the argument arrayBuffer can lead to uncontrolled memory allocation. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A vulnerability was identified in Snes9x up to 1.63. The impacted element is the function S9xUnfreezeFromStream of the file snapshot.cpp of the component Save-State Screenshot Restoration. The manipulation leads to out-of-bounds read. The attack must be carried out locally. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in PLYImporter::LoadFace and PLYImporter::createFromeTriStrip that fails to validate face vertex indices against the vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file whose out-of-range indices cause GenVertexNormalsProcess::GenMeshVertexNormals to write normals outside the heap buffer, crashing the application or potentially enabling code execution.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ReadFloat in ColladaLoader.cpp because accessor stride and offset bounds are checked only by ai_assert. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose animation accessor describes more values than its float_array holds to read past the array or dereference null, crashing the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that uses NORMAL and TEXCOORD accessors without comparing their counts to the POSITION vertex count. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with shorter normal or texture coordinate arrays to trigger heap out-of-bounds reads and writes that crash the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an invalid pointer dereference vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportEmbeddedTextures that derives the texture format hint without checking the strchr result. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file with an embedded image mime type lacking a slash to crash the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use of uninitialized resource vulnerability in glTFImporter::ImportMeshes that builds TRIANGLE_STRIP and TRIANGLE_FAN faces from unfilled faces. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF 1.0 file whose strip or fan primitives trigger out-of-bounds reads or null pointer dereferences, crashing the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ColladaParser::CopyVertex that allows attackers to read heap memory by supplying primitives lacking a VERTEX input. Attackers can provide a crafted Collada file whose SIZE_MAX per-vertex offset bypasses the release-removed ai_assert check, crashing the importing application.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in FBXConverter::GetRotationKeyframeList that allows attackers to exhaust memory via unbounded rotation angle differences. Attackers can supply a crafted FBX file of about 111 KB whose keyframe interpolation loop never advances, consuming gigabytes of memory until the importing process is killed.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ColladaParser::ReadPrimitives that allows attackers to exhaust memory via non-numeric index values. Attackers can supply a crafted Collada file whose

index list contains a non-digit character, causing endless zero-index appends until the importing process crashes.

A security flaw has been discovered in HuLaSpark HuLa up to 3.0.9. This vulnerability affects the function showMsg of the file luohuo-cloud/luohuo-im/luohuo-im-biz/src/main/java/com/luohuo/flex/im/core/chat/service/strategy/msg/RecallMsgHandler.java of the component Recall Message Notification. The manipulation of the argument nickName results in cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in TOTOLINK A7100RU 7.4cu.2313_B20191024. This issue affects the function exportOvpn of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi of the component CGI Handler. This manipulation of the argument Username causes os command injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely.

A security vulnerability has been detected in osCommerce 4.14.63493. Impacted is the function actionOrdersbatch of the file lib/backend/controllers/OrdersController.php of the component Orders Batch Processing. Such manipulation of the argument orders leads to sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in osCommerce up to 4.14.63493. The impacted element is the function actionSuccess of the file lib/frontend/controllers/MultisafeController.php of the component MultiSafepay Payment Success Callback. Executing a manipulation of the argument customer_id can lead to improper authentication. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability has been found in osCommerce up to 4.14.63493. This affects the function actionCached of the file lib/frontend/controllers/ImageController.php of the component Cached Image Handler. The manipulation of the argument image leads to path traversal. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in osCommerce 4.14.63493. This impacts the function get_address_book_data of the file lib/common/helpers/Customer.php of the component Account Address List Widget. The manipulation of the argument customers_id results in sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in osCommerce 4.14.63493. Affected by this vulnerability is the function updateAddress of the file lib/common/components/Customer.php of the component Address Book Handler. Such manipulation of the argument address_book_id leads to authorization bypass. The attack may be launched remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security flaw has been discovered in osCommerce 4.14.63493. Affected by this issue is the function save_products of the file lib/common/classes/extended/OrderAbstract.php of the component Order Placement. Performing a manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in osCommerce 4.14.63493. This affects the function actionGiftCard of the file lib/frontend/controllers/CatalogController.php of the component Virtual Gift Card Basket. Executing a manipulation of the argument products_id can lead to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security vulnerability has been detected in SourceCodester Cosmetics and Beauty Product Online Store 1.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file admin/orders/view_order.php of the component Admin Order Management. The manipulation of the argument ID leads to sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

A vulnerability was identified in chillzhuang SpringBlade up to 5.0.2. This impacts the function AvueIframe of the file src/components/iframe/main.vue of the component Iframe Route Renderer. The manipulation of the argument url leads to cross site scripting. The attack may be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security flaw has been discovered in yangzongzhuan RuoYi up to 4.8.3. Affected is the function renderUserCards of the file ruoyi-admin/src/main/resources/templates/system/role/view.html of the component Role Management User-View. The manipulation of the argument Username results in cross site scripting. The attack may be launched remotely. The patch is identified as 04db82c3c85593921ab8be48a4b3016866eaa97e. It is best practice to apply a patch to resolve this issue.

A weakness has been identified in phpBB up to 3.3.19. Affected by this vulnerability is the function phpbb_get_user_rank of the file includes/acp/acp_ranks.php of the component Ranks Handler. This manipulation of the argument rank_image causes cross site scripting. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor confirms: "We have reviewed the report and intend to address the issue as part of our ongoing security hardening efforts. Given that exploitation requires authenticated administrative access, we consider this a low-priority issue. We will aim to include a fix in our next release and will notify you once it is available."

The dell-xps-touchpad-haptics package before 1.0.0-4 for Omarchy allows local users to change ownership of a root-owned file by making their own .config/omarchy/dell-haptic.conf file a symlink to that target file.

A flaw was found in the GLib DMA-BUF path of WebKitGTK. The UIProcess trusted fds.size() as the DMA-BUF plane count when handling AcceleratedBackingStore::DidCreateDMABufBuffer and copied offsets and strides without verifying that those vectors had the same length. A compromised WebProcess can send mismatched vector lengths, causing an out-of-bounds read in the privileged UIProcess. This can disclose UIProcess memory and crash the UIProcess, and may be used as part of a Web Content sandbox-escape chain.

A vulnerability has been found in KeudellCoding User Location Map up to 1.2.5. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file resources/humhub.usermap.js of the component MapView Widget. The manipulation of the argument displayname leads to cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 1.3.0 addresses this issue. The identifier of the patch is c49a5fcdb289808378836c19d4da199913798a50. The affected component should be upgraded.

A vulnerability was determined in vijaythapa333 django-student-management-system up to 0d96e62cc4e996e3e77bec1b8e3da3980edf8889. This affects the function get_students of the file StaffViews.py of the component Take Attendance Staff Dashboard. This manipulation of the argument first_name causes cross site scripting. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. This product is using a rolling release to provide continious delivery. Therefore, no version details for affected nor updated releases are available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security flaw has been discovered in vijaythapa333 django-student-management-system up to 0d96e62cc4e996e3e77bec1b8e3da3980edf8889. This issue affects the function add_student_save of the file HodViews.py of the component Student Profile Picture Upload. Performing a manipulation of the argument profile_pic results in unrestricted upload. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Missing authorization vulnerability in the "GetByProject" endpoint (/Project/{id}) of the VulnController in Cervantes version v1.3-beta could allow an authenticated attacker with VulnsRead permission to retrieve the vulnerabilities of any project, even without being a member of it, by supplying an arbitrary project ID.

Tolgee before 3.242.5 fails to enforce email verification on the TOTP enable and recovery-code regeneration endpoints, allowing attackers to enroll MFA on unverified accounts via the @BypassEmailVerification annotation. Attackers can register with a victim's email, enroll an attacker-controlled TOTP factor through PUT /v2/user/mfa/totp, and permanently lock the legitimate owner out after verification and password reset.

The weDevs Subscribe2 WordPress plugin 10.35 before 10.50 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remove public subscribers by forging the s2_unsub GET parameter. Attackers can base64-encode a known subscriber email and visit any page with the subscribe2 shortcode to delete that subscriber from the mailing list.

Future AGI before 1.51.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in ACSView.post that allows authenticated members of any organization to take over accounts in other organizations by asserting arbitrary e-mail addresses. Attackers can register a controlled identity provider through IDPUploadViews to obtain sessions as cross-tenant users, and can modify or delete other organizations' identity-provider configurations.

Windmill 1.607.0 before 1.819.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows workspace members to resume or cancel suspended flows in other workspaces by abusing the jobs_u/resume and jobs_u/cancel endpoints. Attackers can mint a resume signature for an arbitrary job id via their own workspace's job_signature endpoint to approve or cancel another workspace's suspended flow steps.

Windmill 1.664.0 before 1.819.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows any workspace member to mint resume signatures for suspended jobs via create_job_signature, get_resume_urls and get_wac_approval_urls handlers. Members with any role, including operator, can obtain valid HMAC-signed resume URLs to approve flow steps despite self_approval_disabled or user_groups_required restrictions.

Interstellar before 6.3.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach internal services by enabling allow_loopback_ips and allow_private_ips in wisp-js at startup. Attackers can open a wisp WebSocket that bypasses the Express password middleware and create TCP streams to loopback, internal hosts, or cloud metadata services.

Sim 0.5.61 before 0.9.41 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows write-level workspace members to change workflow MCP server visibility without admin permission. Attackers can set isPublic via POST or PATCH to /api/mcp/workflow-servers, exposing deployed workflows to unauthenticated invocation through /api/mcp/serve.

Okou API before 1.762.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in its Microsoft Teams, legacy Slack, and GitHub App integration OAuth flows that trusts caller-supplied userId and orgId values. Unauthenticated attackers who know a member's identifiers can complete the flow with their own external account to bind that identity or installation to the victim's Okou user and organization.

Formance Ledger 2.2.0-beta.3 before 2.4.18 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows remote API callers to execute SQL by supplying unvalidated account expand values. Attackers can inject comment-separated SQL through the expand query parameter or base64 pagination cursor to run queries with the ledger database role's privileges.

CISO Assistant before 4.2.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to block all logins by exhausting a shared rate limit keyed on the frontend server IP. Attackers can send a low sustained rate of failed login attempts through the SvelteKit frontend to exhaust the django-allauth per-address budget, locking out every user.

Umbraco CMS 17.4.0 before 17.8.2 and 18.0.0 before 18.3.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because MemberValueSetBuilder.GetValueSets writes sensitive member properties into the Examine members index. Backoffice users with Settings and Members access but outside the Sensitive data group can search the index via the Examine Management dashboard or Management API to read hidden sensitive member values.

LibRaw 0.22.0 through 0.22.3 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in HuffTable::len() because parse_dht() stores Huffman DC symbols without validating them as difference categories. Attackers can supply a crafted TIFF/ARW file with oversized Huffman symbols in a Sony YCbCr lossless JPEG stream to crash applications decoding it, causing denial of service.

msgpack-c C++ library cpp-3.0.0 through cpp-9.0.0, when built with MSGPACK_USE_X3_PARSE, contains an out-of-bounds heap read in x3_parse.hpp due to assuming contiguous input. Attackers can supply msgpack str, bin or ext values unpacked from non-contiguous containers like std::deque, causing memcpy past storage blocks and disclosing adjacent heap memory.

Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a Lua code injection vulnerability that allows LDAP-authenticated users to inject Lua statements into session files via unescaped login names. Attackers can log in with a name containing a Lua long-string terminator followed by code, which executes on a later session request as the Wing FTP service account.

Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a predictable session identifier vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack administrator sessions by deriving identifiers from process, time, ServerID, and client IP state. Attackers can enumerate candidate identifiers using the service_get_license.html endpoint as a validity oracle and replay live sessions to gain administrative control including the Lua console.

Question2Answer through 1.8.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the qa-include/ajax/version.php admin version-check handler that allows authenticated administrators to make the server send arbitrary HTTP GET requests. Attackers can supply a loopback, private-network, or cloud metadata address in the uri POST parameter with isCore=true to read internal service responses returned in the Ajax output.

PdfPig through 0.1.16 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying crafted PDF documents with self-referencing AcroForm /Kids or deeply nested marked content. Attackers can trigger an uncatchable StackOverflowException in AcroFormFactory.GetAcroField or Page.GetOptionalContentsRecursively, terminating any process reading form fields or optional content.

Softaculous Virtualizor before 3.2.9 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in enduser/auth_callback.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication via OAuth-returned email addresses. Attackers can register an OAuth provider account with an email containing SQL syntax to complete social login as the administrator account.

ZITADEL 4.19.5 before 4.20.3 contains a host header injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect notification links by placing a trusted host in the userinfo portion of the x-zitadel-public-host header. Attackers knowing a victim's login name can harvest single-use codes from password-reset links sent to their host, reset passwords, and take over accounts including administrators.

LibRaw 0.22.3 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in LibRaw::xtrans_interpolate() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted X-Trans raw files. When wavelet denoising threshold or chromatic aberration correction is enabled, the destimage buffer is sized from halved iwidth/iheight but indexed at full width, causing writes of file-derived pixel values beyond the allocation and crashes.

LibRaw through 0.22.3 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in LibRaw::pentax_4shot_load_raw() that allows attackers to crash applications by scanning tiff_ifd[] beyond its 10 entries. Attackers can supply a crafted four-frame Pentax DNG with too few IFDs matching the raw dimensions to cause denial of service when LIBRAW_RAWOPTIONS_PENTAX_PS_ALLFRAMES is enabled.

ToDesktop Builder before 0.36.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the todesktop-fs custom protocol handler that allows attackers to escape the bundled files directory using ../ sequences. Attackers who can run script in an application's renderer can issue XMLHttpRequest calls with traversal paths to read arbitrary files accessible to the user.

Healthchecks before 4.4 contains a verification bypass vulnerability that allows project users to mark arbitrary email addresses as verified because Channel.make_token() omits the email address. Attackers can verify an address they control, change the integration to a victim address, then reuse the original link to send unsolicited alert emails.

Kerberos Agent before 3.14.4 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge administrator tokens because JWTMiddleWare() falls back to the hard-coded key TOBECHANGED. Attackers can sign HS256 tokens with arbitrary username and role claims to access /api and /config routes, exposing RTSP, ONVIF, Hub and encryption keys, rewriting configuration, and stopping the camera.

ServerOS Panel before 1.10.1 contains a decompression bomb vulnerability in DeploySourcePacker::extract() that allows authenticated users with manage-machines permission to bypass the 4 GB unpacked-size limit by under-declaring zip entry sizes. Attackers can upload a crafted archive via POST /machines/{machine}/sources whose entries inflate far beyond declared sizes, filling the host disk and denying service to all workspaces.

Plane before 1.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in WorkspaceDraftIssueViewSet that allows authenticated workspace members to create drafts in unauthorized projects by supplying an arbitrary project_id. Attackers can convert drafts into work items in private or removed-from projects with chosen title, state, assignees, cycle_id and module_ids, triggering notifications and disclosing project membership.

BISHENG before 3.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the /api/v2/workflow/invoke and /api/v2/workflow/stop routes that allows unauthenticated attackers to run workflows as the administrator. Attackers knowing a workflow UUID can supply an override replacing a Code node's code parameter with Python passed to exec(), achieving remote code execution, or stop other users' workflow sessions.

AiSOC before 23.6.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the agents service that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' investigation runs by supplying their run_id. Attackers can query GET /api/v1/investigations/{run_id}, report variants, the WebSocket stream, or agent-runs routes to obtain audit logs, forensic output, and incident reports.

Worklenz before 3.4.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /api/v1/activity-logs/:id that allows authenticated users to read other teams' task activity logs because it lacks the verifyTaskAccess middleware. Attackers who know another team's task UUID can retrieve reporter and assignee names and avatars plus the full timeline of status, priority, label and estimation changes.

MISP contains an authorization bypass in the galaxy cluster detachment functionality. Users holding the sync role permission were incorrectly exempted from the tagger and organisation ownership checks when detaching galaxy clusters from events or attributes.

This allowed a sync user belonging to one organisation to remove galaxy cluster associations (threat intelligence tags) from events and attributes owned by a different organisation. The sync permission was intended for replication workflows, which never invoke the cluster detachment code path, but was erroneously used as a blanket authorization bypass.

Impact:
- Cross-organisation data integrity: a sync user can strip threat intelligence cluster associations from other organisations' events and attributes.
- Disruption of shared threat intelligence: removal of cluster tags can alter the analytical context of events visible to other users.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with the sync role permission (perm_sync) and tagger permission (perm_tagger).
- The target event or attribute must belong to a different organisation than the attacker.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP Collections retained a sharing group reference (sharing_group_id) even when the collection's distribution level was below 4 (i.e., not restricted to a sharing group). As a result, the sharing group name and UUID were displayed in the collection index and view endpoints to any user who could see the collection, regardless of whether that user was a member of the sharing group. Additionally, when collections were pushed to remote MISP servers, the sharing group data was included in the push payload even for collections not distributed to a sharing group, potentially leaking the group identity to remote systems.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with sufficient access to view the affected collection (e.g., a collection with distribution 0-3 that is publicly or broadly visible).
- The collection must have a stale sharing_group_id stored from a prior save.

Impact:
- Unauthorized disclosure of the sharing group name and UUID to users outside the group.
- Potential leakage of sharing group structure to remote MISP servers via the push mechanism.
- An attacker could enumerate sharing group names to identify targeting opportunities.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP's interactive CLI shell, when used to edit or disable a user account, did not update the user record's modification timestamp. The application's session validation mechanism relies on this timestamp to detect that a user's record has changed and to reload the user's state in all active sessions.

As a result, a user who was disabled or had their role or permissions modified through the CLI would retain their existing authenticated session and continue to operate with their previous privileges until the session naturally expired. The administrative intent to revoke or reduce access was not enforced on already-active sessions.

Preconditions:
- An administrator performs a user edit or disable action via the MISP interactive CLI shell rather than the web interface.
- The target user has one or more active web sessions at the time of the change.

Impact:
- A disabled user retains full access to the MISP instance for the duration of their existing session.
- A user whose role or permissions were reduced via the CLI continues to operate with their prior, higher privileges in open sessions.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the feed and server event preview pages. When a remote MISP instance (configured as a feed source or connected server) supplies object or reference UUIDs and IDs containing special characters, these values are rendered in the preview HTML without proper escaping.

The vulnerable behavior occurs in two contexts:

- HTML element identifiers and text content: Remote UUIDs and IDs are inserted into DOM element IDs and visible text without HTML encoding, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML markup.
- Inline JavaScript event handlers: Remote UUIDs and IDs are embedded into onClick handler strings using only HTML escaping, which does not protect against JavaScript string-literal breakout. A crafted value containing a single quote can terminate the string and inject arbitrary JavaScript.

An attacker who controls a remote MISP instance (feed or server peer) can craft UUID or ID fields with a malicious payload. When an authenticated user on the victim instance views the corresponding event preview, the injected script executes in the user's browser within the MISP application origin, potentially allowing session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a stored cross-site script (XSS) vulnerability in the event review page used for merge, import, and enrichment workflows.

Object references displayed on this page include the UUID, name, and meta-category of the referenced object. These values originate from imported data (another event, a module result, or an import file) and were rendered into the HTML output without any encoding or sanitization.

An attacker who can supply or influence imported MISP-format data can embed arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the referenced object's UUID, name, or meta-category fields. When a user views the review page, the malicious script executes in the user's browser context.

Preconditions:
- The attacker must be able to introduce data into a MISP instance (e.g., via import, module enrichment, or event merge).
- A victim user must open the affected review page in a browser.

Security impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application.
- Potential theft of session tokens, manipulation of user actions, or exfiltration of sensitive threat-intelligence data visible on the page.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in its map attachment rendering. When a GPX or GeoJSON file is uploaded as an attachment to a MISP event, the waypoint names (GPX) and property names and values (GeoJSON) are inserted into Leaflet map popups without HTML escaping. Because Leaflet renders popup content as raw HTML, any markup or script embedded in those fields is executed in the browser of every user who views the map and interacts with the affected marker or icon.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with permission to upload attachments to a MISP event crafts a GPX or GeoJSON file containing malicious HTML/JavaScript in waypoint names or GeoJSON property keys/values.
- A victim user views the event map and clicks the affected marker or GeoJSON icon, triggering the popup.

Impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the MISP web application, potentially leading to session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the event report element rendering pipeline. The client-side sanitization function used to prepare values for doT templates only escaped ampersand, less-than, and greater-than characters. However, the templates place these values inside double-quoted HTML attributes. Because double-quote and single-quote characters were not escaped, a user with the ability to author or modify report element values could inject a quote character to break out of the attribute context and inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in the viewing user's browser.

Preconditions:
- The attacker must be an authenticated user with permission to create or edit event report elements (e.g., a report author).
- A victim must open or view the crafted report in a browser.

Security impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the victim's MISP session.
- Potential theft of session tokens, sensitive data, or unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Overmind server preview's analyst data badge component. When rendering the analyst data link for a remote attribute, the remote server's UUID value was inserted into an inline JavaScript event handler using only HTML entity encoding, which is insufficient to prevent breakout from the JavaScript string context within the HTML attribute.

An attacker who can control or influence the UUID value of a remote attribute (for example, through a malicious or compromised upstream MISP server sharing data via Overmind) could inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the context of the victim's MISP session when the analyst data badge is clicked.

Preconditions:
- The victim must be authenticated to a MISP instance with Overmind enabled.
- The victim must view a remote event preview containing the crafted UUID.
- The victim must interact with (click) the analyst data badge element.

Security impact:
- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session.
- Potential theft of session credentials, manipulation of page content, or initiation of unauthorized actions on behalf of the authenticated user.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the data capture and import paths for events, galaxies, galaxy clusters, analyst data, and sightings. A user who is neither a sync user nor a site admin could create or import records attributed to an organisation other than their own, or cause the creation of a new organisation from a payload-supplied identifier.

The root cause is an inconsistent authorization check: the code validated one representation of the creator organisation (for example a numeric ID or a UUID field) while storing a different representation taken directly from the user-supplied payload. In the event import path, a MISP export naming another organisation or a fabricated one was accepted and stored under that organisation. In the galaxy, cluster, analyst data, and sighting capture paths, the nested organisation object from the payload was used to create or reference an organisation without verifying the caller's membership.

Impact:
- Data (events, galaxies, clusters, analyst notes, sightings) can be created under an organisation the attacker does not belong to, polluting that organisation's data and potentially exposing it to that organisation's members.
- New organisations can be created from attacker-supplied identifiers, introducing phantom entities into the MISP instance.
- The integrity of the threat-intelligence data store is compromised because attribution is no longer trustworthy.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains an authorization bypass in its tag attachment functionality. The endpoints responsible for editing event tags, editing attribute tags, and adding tags to event reports accepted arbitrary tag IDs without verifying whether the authenticated user was permitted to attach the referenced tag.

The events/addTag endpoint already resolved tag IDs through a restricted lookup that enforced per-user and per-organisation tag visibility rules. However, the three tag-editor endpoints (editEventTags, editAttributeTags, and eventReports/addTag) passed the supplied tag IDs directly to the attachment logic without any such check.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with tagger and add permissions on the target event/attribute/report.
- Knowledge or discovery of a tag ID that is restricted (local_only) to another organisation.

Impact:
- A user can attach a tag that is restricted to a different organisation, effectively bypassing the tag visibility and scoping model.
- A local_only tag can be attached as a global tag, violating the intended distribution restriction and potentially exposing the existence or semantics of another organisation's restricted tag to a broader audience.
- Data integrity of the MISP instance is compromised as the tag association model no longer reflects the intended access-control boundaries.

Affected versions: MISP prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the handling of Galaxy and Galaxy Cluster publish/unpublish operations. The application failed to enforce consistent permission checks when users attempted to unpublish a Galaxy or Galaxy Cluster. Specifically, the unpublish action only required the 'perm_galaxy_editor' permission, whereas the publish action required both 'perm_galaxy_editor' and 'perm_publish'.

This inconsistency allowed a user from a different organization who possessed the 'perm_galaxy_editor' permission but lacked the 'perm_publish' permission to unpublish a Galaxy or Galaxy Cluster created by another organization. This action could disrupt the availability of shared threat intelligence data for other users and organizations relying on that cluster.

The vulnerability affects MISP versions prior to 2.5.52.

MISP contains an authorization flaw in the Sharing Group Blueprint execution path. When a blueprint is executed, it rewrites the organisation roster of the associated sharing group. The check verifying that the blueprint's owning organisation still holds the right to extend (modify) that group was performed only once, at the time the blueprint was created. It was not re-evaluated at execution time.
